derivation_notes: The parent treated rho as translating linearly into realized removable contacts once the trigger is active. Here rho is reinterpreted as nominal intervention intensity, while realized suppression uses rho/(1 + rho) to represent competition between contact removal and overlap/fatigue among increasingly hard-to-remove contacts.
change_summary: The active-regime suppression law is refined so stronger nominal intervention has diminishing realized effect. This preserves baseline behavior near and below the trigger but bends the c_eff-versus-rho relationship at substantial activation.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Compliance is constant whenever the intervention is active.
assumption_audit.mechanism: As intervention intensity increases, removable contacts are exhausted and additional nominal effort increasingly overlaps already-suppressed or resistant contacts, reducing marginal effectiveness.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed c0, p_trigger, and rho, the parent maps prevalence excess above the trigger to a monotone increase in suppression that approaches the single ceiling rho with one fixed diminishing-returns shape.
response_change.child_relation: For fixed c0 and p_trigger, the maximum suppressible fraction itself decreases as rho becomes large, representing overlap and fatigue among removable contacts, so increasing rho yields diminishing realized suppression and a flatter high-rho response even when prevalence is well above trigger.
response_change.observable_effect: At high prevalence above the trigger, c_eff falls roughly linearly with rho in the parent, but in the child the decline with rho bends and saturates because additional nominal intervention strength produces smaller contact reductions.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when prevalence is at or above the trigger and especially for p sufficiently above p_trigger that activation is substantial; the contrast is strongest across moderate-to-large rho where nominal suppression approaches the limit of removable contacts.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, varying rho at fixed p > p_trigger reveals weaker-than-linear gains in suppression; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to stronger active regimes, where the parent keeps scaling with one shared gain but the child saturates in realized effect.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the overlap/fatigue correction to zero so realized suppression becomes proportional to rho throughout the active regime.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: competition between nominal intervention effort and the pool of still-removable contacts
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: As intervention intensity increases, the easiest discretionary contacts are removed first; stronger nominal controls increasingly target contacts already avoided or contacts that are hard to remove, so realized suppression shows diminishing returns with rho.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the functional role of rho from a single linear gain to a competing-process saturation law, altering curvature in the scored mapping across active conditions while preserving the inactive limit.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The current law treats rho as a perfectly effective linear ceiling parameter inside the active regime, implicitly assuming every increment of nominal intervention strength removes a new, non-overlapping set of contacts.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Nominal intervention intensity competes with overlap and fatigue, so realized suppressible contact fraction saturates as rho increases.

evolution_contract.parent_reduction: For weak nominal intervention rho << 1, rho/(1 + rho) ≈ rho, recovering the parent law to leading order throughout the active regime.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Holding c0 and p_trigger fixed, compare conditions with p above the trigger while varying rho. The parent predicts nearly proportional additional suppression with increasing rho at a given activation level, whereas the child predicts concave, saturating reduction in c_eff versus rho; below trigger both remain near c0, so the contrast is specifically an active-regime target-mapping change.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot match both low-rho and high-rho active conditions because the parent is affine in rho after the prevalence-dependent factor is fixed, while the child has intrinsic concavity from rho/(1 + rho). Retuning existing coefficients can shift overall gain or trigger sharpness but cannot create the observed saturation of realized suppression across rho with one shared fit.

evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current law treats rho as a perfectly effective linear ceiling parameter inside the active regime, implicitly assuming every increment of nominal intervention strength removes a new, non-overlapping set of contacts.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Compliance is constant whenever the intervention is active.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: As intervention intensity increases, the easiest discretionary contacts are removed first; stronger nominal controls increasingly target contacts already avoided or contacts that are hard to remove, so realized suppression shows diminishing returns with rho.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent’s constant-compliance interpretation of rho. Hold c0 and p_trigger fixed, and compare policies at the same measured prevalence p above the trigger while varying rho over its admissible range. The parent enforces a single-gain relationship: once active, larger rho always converts proportionally into larger contact suppression up to the same prevalence-dependent factor, so one shared parameterization cannot produce pronounced concavity in c_eff versus rho. The child instead makes realized suppression a saturating function of nominal intervention strength, reflecting overlap among removable contacts and compliance fatigue. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary quantity: at the same observed p, high-rho policies no longer reduce c_eff as much as the parent predicts. The effect is scientifically admissible when intervention is active; below trigger both parent and child should remain near baseline because there is little or no suppression to saturate. This refinement respects nonnegativity and the requirement that stronger intervention not increase contacts, while adding a concrete observable contrast that cannot be absorbed by simply refitting the parent’s existing single rho gain across both low-rho and high-rho active conditions.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Introduce a gain or loss that competes with an existing process in different state regions.

scenario_text: Determine the effective contact rate used by an epidemic-control program that activates when measured prevalence reaches a specified trigger. Below the trigger, contacts remain at their baseline level; at or above it, a fixed fraction of contacts is suppressed. Prevalence, the uncontrolled contact rate, the trigger, and intervention strength are independently sampled policy conditions. The target is the immediate controlled contact rate, without modeling delayed behavioral adjustment.
